the-test-behind-every-visitor-visa-a-gen.h2: The test behind every visitor visa

blocks.x: The Department of Home Affairs must be satisfied that you intend to visit Australia temporarily and then leave. This is the genuine temporary stay test in clause 600.211 of Schedule 2 to the Migration Regulations. The decision maker looks at your whole situation. No single document guarantees a grant.

head: What they look at
Evidence that helps
rows: Employer letter with approved leave and return date, recent payslips and tax returns, business registration if self-employed, proof of study
Recent bank statements showing steady funds, an explanation for any large or recent deposits, evidence of assets
Close family who stay at home, a travel history that shows you followed visa conditions

visa-conditions-that-catch-visitors-out.h2: Visa conditions that catch visitors out

items.x: **Condition 8101 (no work).** You cannot work in Australia on a standard visitor visa.
**Condition 8201 (study limit).** Study is limited to 3 months.
**Condition 8503 (no further stay).** You cannot apply for most other visas while you are in Australia. A waiver is only given in limited, compelling cases.
**Condition 8558 (stay limit).** You cannot stay more than 12 months in any 18-month period.

blocks.x: Breaking a condition can lead to cancellation and make later visa applications harder. Check your grant letter for the conditions on your visa.

common-reasons-visitor-visas-are-refused.h2: Common reasons visitor visas are refused

items.x: Weak ties to home, such as no job, no leave approval or no close family there.
Savings that do not match the trip, or unexplained deposits.
A vague itinerary, or one that does not match the stated purpose.
A history of overstays, refusals or breaches that was not explained.
A sponsor or host who has not shown their own status or relationship.
Answers on the form that do not match your documents.

blocks.x: A refusal stays on your record and is asked about in later applications. If you were refused, read our [visa refusal page](/appeals/visa-refusal) before you reapply. Our registered migration agents review your evidence, tell you honestly if it is thin and prepare a cover submission that addresses the genuine temporary stay test. We cannot guarantee any visa outcome.

if-you-are-new-what-now.h2: If you are new, what now?

blocks.x: The 188 and 132 are not open to new applicants, so there is no business or investor visa to apply for under those programs. Which visa suits you depends on your skills, age, family and plans. Options include:

items.x: **Skilled visa.** If your occupation is on a relevant list. See [skilled migration](/migrate-to-australia).
**Employer-sponsored visa.** See [employer-sponsored visas](/employer-sponsored). A business-owner route may suit some people.
**Partner or family visa.** If you have a qualifying relationship. See [family visas](/family-visa).
**Student visa, then a graduate visa.** If you plan to study first. See [Study in Australia](/study-australia).
**National Innovation Visa (subclass 858).** It replaced the Global Talent visa and is invitation-only, for people with a record of outstanding achievement.

blocks.x: We do not promise a pathway. A registered agent can tell you what is realistic.

the-deadline-is-in-your-decision-letter-.h2: The deadline is in your decision letter. Find it first.

items.x: **Check the letter.** It says whether you can ask for review, who can review the decision and how long you have.
**The clock may already be running.** Time is counted from when you are taken to have received the notice, not from when you read it.

**Different decisions have different limits.** Refusals, cancellations, decisions made in immigration detention and court review each have their own time limit. Your letter, or an agent, can tell you which applies to you.
**Do not assume a late application will be accepted.** Call us as soon as you have the letter.

blocks.label: Note
blocks.x: Do not wait until the last week. Evidence takes time to collect.

what-to-do-in-the-first-48-hours.h2: What to do in the first 48 hours

items.x: **Find the deadline.** Read your decision letter and write the date and time limit where you can see it.
**Call us on +61 3 9602 1330.** Do this today, even if you have not gathered everything. A registered migration agent will read your letter and tell you what to do next.
**Keep every letter and email** from the Department of Home Affairs. Do not ignore anything.
**Check your visa status.** Look at your visa expiry, any bridging visa and your work or study conditions. Do not travel, sign anything or change your plans before you speak to an agent.
**Gather your paperwork.** Decision letter, copy of your application, passport pages, evidence you sent and emails from the Department.
**Do not rely on social media advice.** Forum answers are often out of date or wrong for your visa type.
